    - I know your face. No, I know your nose. Somebody's grandmother had that nose. It'll come to me. It always does, usually at the worst moment.
    - Ah, *Player*. The one who made Kite admit I was right. I've told everyone. Twice. Saucer read it in my tea leaves before you even went. Saucer says that sort of thing.
    - *Player*! Ozzie wrote it down properly. With the ribbon. I made him read it back to me three times. I cried at the same bit each time. That's how you know a story's right.
    - Well? Ask. I've got till the lanterns come on.

    - Posy. A baby of a few months, on the day of the Long Walk. Her mother, my grandmother Marguerite, was a lace-maker that no Selsior guild would let in. So she packed her lace bobbins round the baby in a laundry basket, and walked.
    - Out of the gates of Selsior in a basket, and all the way here. That is the most important fact about this city, and don't let anyone at the Table tell you otherwise. The Charter's all very well. My mother was in a basket.
    - The tannery roof, the one with the green slates: fell in when I was six. The baker's lean-to by the Old Barracks: patched by a man who drank. The long one over the Night Market that Kite likes to jump: sound as a drum, but the gutter's rotten on the north end. You heard me. North end.
    - Never had any children. Outlived a husband and two sweethearts, all lovely, all dead. About forty years ago the square started calling me Nana and I couldn't make it stop. And Gristle because I'm tough as it. Try me.
    - Go on, then. And eat something. You look like Rook.
